text:
oliver.m: Hey all, day 1 and stuck. I accepted the org invite and I'm showing as Member, but I can't push to any repos and `gh repo list --private` returns nothing. I can still see internal docs in the wiki, weird. Any ideas?

irene.hr: welcome @oliver.m! Did you recently change your GitHub username or merge accounts? That can cause the org to have a stale mapping.

oliver.m: Yes actually I changed my username from oliverm-old to oliver-m last month. Could that be it?

it-admin: Possibly. GitHub's SCIM mapping and org membership sometimes reference the old login. Can you run `gh api /user --jq .login` and `gh api /users/oliverm-old` to see if both exist?

oliver.m: `gh api /user --jq .login` -> "oliver-m". `gh api /users/oliverm-old` returns 404. So the old account seems gone.

devops-lead: If the old login was renamed, GitHub should have migrated membership, but if the rename happened recently and the org uses SCIM provisioning or SAML mapping, the SCIM record might still point to the old external_id. We can check org membership API: `gh api /orgs/redwood-inference/memberships/oliver-m` — what does that return?
\ioliver.m: Running it now: returns {"state":"active","role":"member","url":"https://api.github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/memberships/oliver-m","company":null} but I still don't see team membership or private repos.

it-admin: Hmm membership shows active but no teams — two possibilities: 1) GitHub retained membership but lost team links due to rename; 2) your account email isn't verified with the canonical work email, so team SCIM sync skipped you. Check Settings -> Emails and verify your work address is present and verified.
\ioliver.m: My account email lists oliver.m@personal.dev and oliver@redwood.work (unverified). I accepted the invite via the work forwarding address while the work email wasn't verified because AD wasn't fully set up. Could that cause teams not to apply?

devops-lead: Yes — SCIM/group sync often keys off the verified primary email or external_id. If your work address isn't verified, the IdP might not match you to the Okta group. Two fixes: verify your work email then trigger an IdP->SCIM sync; or org admin can remove and re-add you to the correct team manually.
\iirene.hr: I'll flag this with infra. Also reminder: when changing usernames, verify emails before accepting any org invites to avoid edge cases.
\it-admin: Creating ticket now: "username rename + unverified work email -> member without teams". We'll ask infra to force a SCIM sync and confirm team assignment. In the meantime I can add you to the infra team manually so you can push.
\iounvite-bot: Ticket #4988 created: "username rename + unverified email caused missing team assignments" assigned to infra-admins. ETA: 2 hours.
\ioliver.m: Thanks all. I'll verify the work email and hang tight. Appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup!
